clue.text: Included, to be fair, a quarter of the country

indicators.note: the country is said to be included in the run of words that follows, so its letters sit inside them

explanation.surface: Someone admits, in fairness, that a quarter of a nation was taken in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Included' points into 'fair, a quarter', where faIR A Quarter holds the country; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is a Middle Eastern nation, an example of a country.

clue.text: It is mainly to the east of southern Africa

definitions.text: It is mainly to the east of southern Africa

parts.words: It is mainly to the east of southern Africa
parts.note: 'mainly' hints at the main, the sea: the body of water lying off the east coast of southern Africa

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' is a pun on 'the main', an old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The great sea stretching east from Mozambique and South Africa towards Australia is the third-largest ocean.

definitions.meaning: one is a figure, a numeral
a tranquilliser is something that makes you more numb, read as numb plus -er

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading needs the word said as 'numm-er': a thing that numbs, which a tranquilliser does.
explanation.definitionFit: One is a numeral; a tranquilliser is a drug that deadens feeling, a 'more numb' maker.

clue.text: One of no importance is aware that it is a total secret

parts.note: a person of no importance is a nobody
to be aware of something is to know it

explanation.surface: An insignificant person knows a secret, which hardly makes it top secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' is a link between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom said of something no one has found out, a complete mystery.

clue.text: Treat badly when erato, say, is included

indicators.note: the word is is said to be included, so it goes inside the other piece

parts.note: Erato is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, the Muse of love poetry; 'say' marks her as an example

explanation.surface: Mistreatment happens whenever a certain Greek figure is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Erato is the Muse of love poetry in Greek myth; 'say' marks her as one example of a Muse. 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To misuse something or someone is to handle them wrongly or abusively.

parts.note: a circle has no end, and a band of stones set all the way round a finger symbolises endless time

explanation.walkthrough: An eternity ring is a band set with gems all the way round; the clue reads both as a jewel and as time without end.
explanation.definitionFit: Endless time, without beginning or close, is what an unbroken circle stands for.

clue.text: Copper Jack brought back from island

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: brought back means the sailor's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a jack (jack tar) is a sailor, and AB, able seaman, is the usual abbreviation for one

explanation.surface: A policeman named Jack returns from somewhere overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is a Caribbean nation that is an island.

parts.note: lay is an old word for a song, so a lay group is a band of singers in a church, not a body of laity

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' seems to mean not ordained, the congregation; it is a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of singers who lead the music in a cathedral or church service.

clue.text: Buddhist priest right to leave medal

indicators.note: the letter for right is told to leave, so it is taken out of the medal

parts.note: a bronze is the medal for third place

explanation.surface: A monk is told to give up a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonze is a Buddhist monk of East Asia, especially Japan or China.

parts.note: Ron is the short form of the name Ronald
to do is to perform or carry out

explanation.surface: A man named Ronald is set to perform a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a composition in which a main theme keeps returning between contrasting episodes.

indicators.note: troubled means stirred up, so the letters of the two words before are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A dog is causing great numbers of people bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges THOUSANDS BE; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A basset hound is a short-legged breed of hunting hound with long ears.

parts.note: to go is to leave, to quit
a round shape, a circle, is the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone is told to tour a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go round' reads as one instruction to travel about; it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Quito is the capital city of Ecuador.

parts.note: the late are the dead, so getting them up means digging a buried body out of the grave

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a lie-in; 'late' means deceased and 'got up' means raised from the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhumed: a corpse removed from its burial place.

clue.text: Said too much it was not true

definitions.meaning: overstated, put more strongly than the facts allow
describing a claim that was untrue because it was blown up beyond reality

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one confession; it splits into two descriptions of an overstatement.
explanation.definitionFit: Overstated: made out to be bigger or worse than the reality, and so not accurate.

clue.text: Possibly second sequence given by buyer

parts.note: a repeat is a second showing or occurrence, one example of 'second'
an order is a sequence or arrangement

explanation.surface: A second series might be offered by a shopper.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the thing a buyer gives a supplier: a further request for the same goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A request to a supplier for more of the same goods already bought once is a repeat order.

clue.text: Large number of towns, one in south Africa

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
urban means of or relating to towns

explanation.surface: Lots of towns, one of them in the south of the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' stands for a town, so the definition is a town in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Durban is a port city on the east coast of South Africa.

clue.text: Southern church is getting over first major split

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting over means the piece before sits above the next one
first means only the opening letter of the word major is used

explanation.surface: A southern church faces its first big rift.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a division, especially one within a church.

clue.text: One in unusually rocky environment was hoarse

indicators.note: one thing put in another, here the article goes inside the jumbled word
an environment surrounds, so the jumbled word wraps around the single letter
unusually means arranged in an odd way, so the letters of rocky are shuffled

parts.note: one is the indefinite article a

explanation.surface: Someone stuck among rough rocks lost their voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' shuffles ROCKY to CROKY, and 'in ... environment' puts A inside it; 'was' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Croaky describes a rough, husky voice, like a frog's croak.

clue.text: Energetic worker way ahead of modern musician

indicators.note: ahead of means the first piece comes in front of the second

parts.note: ST, street, is a road or way
a rapper performs rap, a modern style of music

explanation.surface: A hard grafter leads the way for a contemporary performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A strapper is a strong, robust person, or one who grooms horses: a vigorous worker.

indicators.note: sounding means the words for a more senior person are said aloud

parts.note: someone more senior is an older man

explanation.surface: A local official seems, by name, to be one of the elders.
explanation.definitionFit: An alderman is a senior member of a town or city council.

parts.note: sticky here means on a stick, not gluey: a frozen treat held by its stick

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticky' suggests toffee; it means mounted on a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen flavoured water lolly on a stick, what Americans call a popsicle.

indicators.note: troublesome suggests disorder, so the letters of Guiana are mixed up

explanation.surface: A tiresome lizard in the South American country of Guiana.
explanation.definitionFit: An iguana is a large tropical American lizard.

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a musical work
a pose is an attitude or posture

explanation.surface: Someone displays an anti-work stance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'anti-work'; the split is 'Have anti' then 'work'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be anti something is to be against it, to resist it.

clue.text: Colliery brush used to clear explosives

parts.note: a colliery is a coal mine
a sweeper is a brush or broom

explanation.surface: A coal-pit broom is put to work on bombs.
explanation.definitionFit: A minesweeper is a ship that clears an area of sea of mines.

indicators.note: one thing hid another, so the climber's letters wrap around gold

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A climbing plant concealed a golden key.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano keys were traditionally faced with ivory, so the ivories, or an ivory, are keys.

indicators.note: not having means the river letter is left out of the word

parts.note: to last is to endure

explanation.surface: The final supply comes without a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to provide or furnish someone with a quality.

parts.note: a pointed missile used in attack, or a sign that points the way

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a military target; the clue is the weapon itself, a pointed missile.
explanation.definitionFit: An archer's shaft with a sharp tip, fired from a bow at an enemy.

parts.note: TT, for total abstainer, marks a teetotaller

explanation.surface: A strong team includes a non-drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Powerful unit' is a unit of power.
explanation.definitionFit: The watt is the SI unit of power.

parts.note: a phrase for poor solace, which is also the title of a comic novel set at a farm

explanation.walkthrough: Stella Gibbons's 1932 comic novel is Cold Comfort Farm; the phrase itself means little consolation.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means meagre solace; add 'Farm' and it is the novel's title.

parts.note: to throw out with force, as a pilot does when the seat shoots out of a jet

explanation.walkthrough: A fighter pilot escapes by the ejector seat; 'perhaps' marks the plane as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel or throw out with force.

clue.text: Extra run included in farm accommodation

indicators.note: included means the letter for run is put inside the extra

parts.note: in cricket a bye is an extra, a run scored without the bat touching the ball
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A further cricket run is fitted into a farm building.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a BYE is an extra scored when the ball passes the batsman untouched.
explanation.definitionFit: A byre is a cowshed, housing for cattle.

indicators.note: a misapprehension is a mistaken grasp, so the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone did not read something because of a mistaken belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Unread describes a book or letter that nobody has looked through.
